To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the plasticity of intrinsic neuronal properties during cell-autonomous maintenance of calcium homeo-stasis is sensitive to the target concentration of intracellular calcium ions and to the strength of afferent inputs.

the evolution of calcium-homeostasis in hippocampal pyramids is sensitive to the type of a priori activity, to the frequency of activity, and to the target calcium level, and that the evolution of intrinsic properties and firing response is sensitive to the target level of calcium and to the strength of the afferent activity, but not the frequency of activity.

(1) calcium homeostasis emerges through cell-autonomous self-regulation in a population of model neurons and (2) state-dependent switches in patterns of synaptic activity result in variable evolution of neuronal intrinsic properties and firing responses, which are sensitive to the strength of afferent inputs, the type of atherent activity and the target calcium concentration.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interplay of homeostasis and neural coding, and how this interplay may impact the evolution of intrinsic properties during neural computation.
understanding how the nervous system can reconcile the maintenance of homeostasis with the perpetual switching of afferent inputs.
understanding the impact of state-dependence on the evolution of neuronal calcium homeostasis, in the context of the hippocampal formation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the intrinsic neuronal properties and firing responses of the model neurons were highly variable and sensitive to the type and strength of the afferent activity, the frequency and the target calcium concentration, and also to the temporal order of switches between the two types of afferent activities.
the evolution of calcium regulation in neurons is a complex process with many facets and that the impact on intrinsic properties and the firing behavior is not a straightforward consequence.

the evolution of calcium-dependent plasticity in a neuron is not a deterministic process, but rather depends on several factors, such as the type of a priori calcium homeostasis, the strength and frequency at which the neuron is driven, and the type and duration of afferent inputs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the evolution of calcium concentration in a neuron depends on the frequency and strength of afferent synaptic inputs.
the evolution of calcium regulation in neurons, in response to afferent activity, is highly variable across neurons, and is sensitive to the strength, frequency, and type of the afferent activity.

, although neurons can adapt their intrinsic properties in response to afferent activity to maintain calcium homeostasis, the nature and degree of this adaptation is variable, and can be sensitive to the nature of the afferent activity, and to the target calcium homeostasis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the evolution of calcium regulation in a population of neurons is not deterministic, and that it is highly sensitive to the type of aferent input and the target calcium concentration.
state-dependent plasticity of intrinsic properties during calcium homeostasis can be a source of variability in neuronal firing responses.
the maintenance of calcium concentration homeostasis is not a simple process that can be described by a single set of conductance changes.
